acceptance: A failure table by job and cause with run IDs covers the window.
The top cause is fixed or moved to a recorded, scheduled lane.
Seven days after the fix, the docs PR failure rate is reported against the 22% baseline.
context:
Triage landed in #2161 on 2026-09-17 as `_project/analysis/docs-failure-triage-2026-09-17.md`, with per-job and per-cause tables over the 2026-08-23 to 2026-09-16 window.

Post-repair measurement, 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-24, from the Actions runs API: `docs.yml` pull_request runs were 237 success, 20 failure, 42 cancelled, 1 running. The failure rate is 20 of 257 completed runs, 7.8%, against the 22% baseline (144 of 662). Counting all 299 runs including cancelled gives 6.7%. The drop corroborates the triage finding that the actionable in-window causes - dead comparison links and bot-gated hosts - were already repaired during the window.

The triage deliberately changed nothing in the workflow: the remaining dominant class, visual comparison failing on related but unapproved page changes, is the gate working as designed on a non-required check, and narrowing it would re-scope a reviewed gate.

Open follow-up, explicitly deferred by the triage to its own review and not part of this item: if the visual red rate stays near 100 failures per 25 days with approvals still bypassed, decide between keeping the friction as the price of the approval flow, scoping comparison to runs touching site-rendered paths, or making visual a required check so its failures must be approved or fixed.
description:
Between 2026-08-23 and 2026-09-16, `docs.yml` failed on 144 of 662 pull_request runs (22%) and 20 of 264 develop pushes. It is not a required check, so these red results create noise and reruns without blocking merges. Per-job causes and runner-minutes were not collected.

Change: classify the failures by job and cause, then fix the dominant causes or narrow the path filter where a failure class is unrelated to the changed files.
